The atlas is unanimous for Microtubule destabilizers (10/10 neighbours, 3/4 wells, e10), and tubulin loss (tub_mean z≈-9 at 0.3-3 µM) with act_tub_ratio z≈+43 fits that class directly. data.note:
Reflection: Specimen s_66b994c89e unblinded as nocodazole (PubChem CID 4122, CHEMBL9514, BBBC021 annotates Microtubule destabilizers; ChEMBL no curated mechanism) — consensus microtubule depolymerizer.

Initial blinded conclusion favored Aurora kinase inhibitors (0.58) based on composite-only micronuclei/grape-like multinucleation, low solidity/form factor and high frac_large_nucleus with preserved mitotic-like=0. PI review correctly noted this over-weighted split microscopist reads (e4/e15 Aurora vs e5/e14 Actin disruptors) vs unanimous atlas: 10/10 neighbours and 3/4 wells Microtubule destabilizers (e10), with dose-dependent tubulin loss (tub_mean +1.47 at 0.1µM to -9.34 at 0.3µM, rho -1.0 for tub_glcm_contrast e22) and extreme act_tub_ratio z~+43. Requested 0.03µM discriminator well could not be acquired (budget exhausted), requiring free-tool reassessment; hypotheses updated to Microtubule destabilizers 0.62, which scored correct.

Literature supports nocodazole as prototypical microtubule destabilizer triggering spindle checkpoint PMID 14614453, with microtubule-targeted drug sensitivity modulation PMID 15389625. Multinucleation/polyploidy is expected secondary to prolonged mitotic failure after microtubule depolymerization, not specific to Aurora inhibition, explaining visual overlap. Future work: sub-threshold dose-response (0.01-0.03µM) + tubulin polymerization and p-H3 Ser10 assays to separate primary tubulin loss from secondary cytokinesis failure.

reflection.text:
After unblinding this was nocodazole, PubChem CID 4122, ChEMBL CHEMBL9514, with identity check name and BBBC021 structure agree e25, e26. ChEMBL lists no curated mechanism, so ground truth had to be inferred phenotypically. Verdict correct: final call Microtubule destabilizers p=0.62 e24 matches truth_moa Microtubule destabilizers, after an initial incorrect call Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.58 e19. PMID 14614453 describes nocodazole as a microtubule destabilizer, consistent with the unblinded structure.

What the evidence got right:
- The reference atlas comparison was the most robust signal. Over 2 wells NSC 1/2 destabilizer but k-neighbour 9/10 destabilizer, 1/10 stabilizer e6, and over 4 wells NSC 3/4 destabilizer and k-neighbour 10/10 destabilizer e10. This unanimous k-NN vote persisted despite single-replicate wells.
- Quantitative features consistently fit tubulin loss: act_tub_ratio z=+32.3 at 1uM e2, z=+20.1 at 0.1uM e3, z=+44.3 at 0.3uM e8, z=+43.4 at 3uM e9; nuc_solidity z=-30.4 e2, -24.2 e3, -35.5 e8, -20.3 e9 and nuc_form_factor z=-24.2 e2. Dose_response e22 tub_glcm_contrast rho=-1.00 p=0 over 4 wells supports contrast loss with dose, complementing tub_mean rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e16. Act_mean elevated z=+23.7 e3, +21.3 e8, +19.2 e9 with dose rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e17 also fit act_tub_ratio increase, not primary actin disruption.
- The acquisition plan was transparent: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.001-3uM but only 4 of 4 wells left e1, so we sampled 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3uM e2,e3,e8,e9. The review correctly flagged this as already saturated.

What misled and why:
- Composite-only microscopist reads were split and over-weighted: e4 density similar, 5 observations candidates Aurora and e15 density lower, 6 observations candidates Aurora vs e5 density lower, 4 observations candidates Actin disruptors and e14 density lower, 6 observations candidates Actin disruptors. Grape-like micronuclei / low solidity/form factor was interpreted as cytokinesis failure of Aurora inhibition, but as the review noted e4/e15 vs e5/e14 split shows observer variability and multinucleation can be secondary to mitotic/microtubule failure.
- Dose-response interpretations on saturated, single-replicate wells were over-confident: frac_mitotic_like was constant across 4 wells e11 and was used to argue zero mitotic arrest contradicts destabilizer arrest, but review correctly called this a flat z-score argument and e15 noted more rounded condensed cells. frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e13 and frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e12 were non-significant, and nuc_solidity rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e20 and act_mean rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e17 likewise p>0.05. Only cell_count rho=+1.00 p=0 e21 and tub_glcm_contrast rho=-1.00 p=0 e22 were significant, but with n=4 single wells they reflect the saturated high-dose window, not a discriminant.
- Hypothesis history shows the flip: step 7 Aurora 0.45 vs destabilizer 0.40 e7, step 18 Aurora 0.58 vs destabilizer 0.32 e18 based on e2,e4,e8,e11,e13,e15 vs e6,e10, then after the critique step 23 destabilizer 0.62 vs Aurora 0.28 e23 based on e10,e8,e9,e16,e22 vs e4,e15. The first submit e19 weighed morphology over the unanimous atlas 10/10 neighbours.

Acquisition choice that mattered:
- By spending the 4-well budget on 0.1-3uM we left no well to test the review's discriminator below the saturated range. The requested experiment was dose index 3, 0.03uM rep 1: preserved tubulin with multinucleation/large nuclei would favour Aurora, primary tubulin loss/act_tub rise with destabilizer atlas match before polyploidy would favour destabilizer. Conclusion e24 was submitted with acquisition blocked for that reason. The lesson is to include a sub-threshold dose when nuclear-shape effects are already maximal at 0.1uM e3,e20.

Literature in this run supported nocodazole as microtubule destabilizer PMID 14614453, and the two PubMed searches e27 48 hits 5 returned for nocodazole microtubule destabilizer and e28 0 hits for destabilizer vs Aurora multinucleation illustrate that literature alone did not resolve the phenotypic overlap.
No clinical implications are inferred; this is cell-biology screening data only.

Verdict: request experiment.

Do not approve: the runner-up explains the ledger at least as well. The atlas is unanimous for Microtubule destabilizers (10/10 neighbours, 3/4 wells, e10), and tubulin loss (tub_mean z≈-9 at 0.3-3 µM) with act_tub_ratio z≈+43 fits that class directly. The Aurora case rests on composite-only phenotype reads that are split (e4/e15 Aurora vs e5/e14 Actin disruptors), and grape-like multinucleation can be secondary to mitotic/microtubule failure. The 'zero mitotic fraction' argument is weak: it is a flat z-score across single-replicate wells (e11) and e15 notes more rounded condensed cells. All doses are single wells (rep 1) and already saturated for nuclear-shape effects, so 0.58 for Aurora over a unanimous atlas call is overconfident.

Requested: Acquire one well at dose index 3 (0.03 µM, replicate 1), below the current saturated range, then run the free atlas comparison and phenotype description on it. Discriminator: multinucleation/large nuclei with preserved tubulin at this sub-threshold dose would favour Aurora kinase inhibitors; primary tubulin loss/act_tub rise with a destabilizer atlas match before polyploidy would favour Microtubule destabilizers.

## Reflection

After unblinding this was nocodazole, PubChem CID 4122, ChEMBL CHEMBL9514, with identity check name and BBBC021 structure agree e25, e26. ChEMBL lists no curated mechanism, so ground truth had to be inferred phenotypically. Verdict correct: final call Microtubule destabilizers p=0.62 e24 matches truth_moa Microtubule destabilizers, after an initial incorrect call Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.58 e19. PMID 14614453 describes nocodazole as a microtubule destabilizer, consistent with the unblinded structure.

What the evidence got right:
- The reference atlas comparison was the most robust signal. Over 2 wells NSC 1/2 destabilizer but k-neighbour 9/10 destabilizer, 1/10 stabilizer e6, and over 4 wells NSC 3/4 destabilizer and k-neighbour 10/10 destabilizer e10. This unanimous k-NN vote persisted despite single-replicate wells.
- Quantitative features consistently fit tubulin loss: act_tub_ratio z=+32.3 at 1uM e2, z=+20.1 at 0.1uM e3, z=+44.3 at 0.3uM e8, z=+43.4 at 3uM e9; nuc_solidity z=-30.4 e2, -24.2 e3, -35.5 e8, -20.3 e9 and nuc_form_factor z=-24.2 e2. Dose_response e22 tub_glcm_contrast rho=-1.00 p=0 over 4 wells supports contrast loss with dose, complementing tub_mean rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e16. Act_mean elevated z=+23.7 e3, +21.3 e8, +19.2 e9 with dose rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e17 also fit act_tub_ratio increase, not primary actin disruption.
- The acquisition plan was transparent: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.001-3uM but only 4 of 4 wells left e1, so we sampled 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3uM e2,e3,e8,e9. The review correctly flagged this as already saturated.

What misled and why:
- Composite-only microscopist reads were split and over-weighted: e4 density similar, 5 observations candidates Aurora and e15 density lower, 6 observations candidates Aurora vs e5 density lower, 4 observations candidates Actin disruptors and e14 density lower, 6 observations candidates Actin disruptors. Grape-like micronuclei / low solidity/form factor was interpreted as cytokinesis failure of Aurora inhibition, but as the review noted e4/e15 vs e5/e14 split shows observer variability and multinucleation can be secondary to mitotic/microtubule failure.
- Dose-response interpretations on saturated, single-replicate wells were over-confident: frac_mitotic_like was constant across 4 wells e11 and was used to argue zero mitotic arrest contradicts destabilizer arrest, but review correctly called this a flat z-score argument and e15 noted more rounded condensed cells. frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e13 and frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e12 were non-significant, and nuc_solidity rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e20 and act_mean rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e17 likewise p>0.05. Only cell_count rho=+1.00 p=0 e21 and tub_glcm_contrast rho=-1.00 p=0 e22 were significant, but with n=4 single wells they reflect the saturated high-dose window, not a discriminant.
- Hypothesis history shows the flip: step 7 Aurora 0.45 vs destabilizer 0.40 e7, step 18 Aurora 0.58 vs destabilizer 0.32 e18 based on e2,e4,e8,e11,e13,e15 vs e6,e10, then after the critique step 23 destabilizer 0.62 vs Aurora 0.28 e23 based on e10,e8,e9,e16,e22 vs e4,e15. The first submit e19 weighed morphology over the unanimous atlas 10/10 neighbours.

Acquisition choice that mattered:
- By spending the 4-well budget on 0.1-3uM we left no well to test the review's discriminator below the saturated range. The requested experiment was dose index 3, 0.03uM rep 1: preserved tubulin with multinucleation/large nuclei would favour Aurora, primary tubulin loss/act_tub rise with destabilizer atlas match before polyploidy would favour destabilizer. Conclusion e24 was submitted with acquisition blocked for that reason. The lesson is to include a sub-threshold dose when nuclear-shape effects are already maximal at 0.1uM e3,e20.

Literature in this run supported nocodazole as microtubule destabilizer PMID 14614453, and the two PubMed searches e27 48 hits 5 returned for nocodazole microtubule destabilizer and e28 0 hits for destabilizer vs Aurora multinucleation illustrate that literature alone did not resolve the phenotypic overlap.
No clinical implications are inferred; this is cell-biology screening data only.

What was right:
- Atlas k-NN 9/10 then 10/10 destabilizer e6 e10 and NSC 3/4 e10 persisted despite single replicates
- act_tub_ratio +32.3 to +44.3 and nuc_solidity -20 to -35.5 across e2 e3 e8 e9 plus tub_glcm_contrast rho -1.00 p=0 e22 fit tubulin loss
- Review critique correctly identified saturated high-dose sampling from e1 budget and split microscopist e4 e15 vs e5 e14 and weak constant mitotic fraction e11

What was wrong or missed:
- Initial p=0.58 Aurora e19 over-weighted grape-like micronuclei/low solidity from e4 e15 vs unanimous atlas e10
- Interpreted constant frac_mitotic_like e11 and non-significant frac_large_nucleus rho+0.80 p0.2 e13 as Aurora polyploidy proof
- Acquired only 0.1-3uM e2 e3 e8 e9 leaving no discriminator 0.03uM as requested in review
